risks: The documentation exclusion is a real hole by design: inside the gated compilations a doc comment can name any guarded type or member from any method, including a decoy, and no rule proves documentation stays off a forbidden path. It is bounded by the fact that a cref produces no operation and the compiler still requires it to bind (CS1574, an error under `TreatWarningsAsErrors`), but it is a hole and it is the price of preserving the three live links unchanged.

`AnalyzerRunner` parses with `CSharpParseOptions.Default`, whose `DocumentationMode` is `Parse` — measured sufficient for crefs to exist and bind. If a future change ever passed `DocumentationMode.None`, every documentation test would pass vacuously without exercising the exclusion. Mitigated by each documentation test asserting the fixture actually produced a `CrefSyntax` node first; the risk survives only if that assertion is removed.

The written-name lens fires `GetSymbolInfo` on every `IdentifierName` and `GenericName` in the gated compilations — `guard`, `AgentGuard.TestHelpers` and `AgentGuard.Engine`. The cref test is syntactic and runs first, and only three compilations are gated, but build time on those three should be compared before and after and reported rather than assumed unchanged.

`NameBinding.Resolve` returns `ITypeSymbol?`, and `AttributeIdentity` narrows it with `as INamedTypeSymbol`. A future caller that forgets the narrowing silently drops array and pointer cases; a future caller that keeps it on a general name silently drops array and pointer coverage. Nothing in the type system stops either — only the direct scanner tests do.

`ILocalSymbol.ContainingSymbol` is measured correct for a local in a method body, a lambda and a local function. It is not measured for a local inside a lambda in a field or property initializer, or under top-level statements. Engine has none today; a fixture covering the field-initializer lambda should be added rather than assuming the answer.

The architecture tests compile the analyzer project's own `netstandard2.0` sources against the net10.0 assemblies loaded in the test process. The zero-error gate makes any mismatch loud rather than silent, but a future package or TFM bump can turn that gate red for a reason unrelated to the design, and the failure will read as an ownership failure unless the test message says otherwise.

`CallerLocationAnswerMustBeUsed` proves the owner's answer is not discarded; it does not prove the analyzer reports correctly, and it does not catch a result assigned to a local that is then never read. The behavioural Acceptance-12 and decoy-call-site fixtures are the only proof of correctness, so weakening either set removes the real guard while the architecture test still passes.

The three one-door rules now register three lenses each on the Engine gate, so one statement can produce two or three diagnostics. The contract forbids cross-lens deduplication, so every count in the four test classes must be computed from the lens matrix; an `Assert.Single` anywhere in them will pass today and hide a lens that stopped firing tomorrow.

`PlatformFactory.Is` anchors AG0029's door on namespace plus name (`WellKnownType.Is`), not on the declaring assembly; the per-OS assembly scope gate covers the assembly half for the callee. That is existing behaviour and out of scope here, but the AG0029 decoy tests must be written against that actual shape rather than assuming `IsInAssembly`, or they will assert something the rule does not do.

Neither is in Surfaces today.

=====================================================================
A. WHAT I MEASURED, AND WHERE
=====================================================================

Everything below was run outside the repository, in a throwaway net9.0 console project pinned to `Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.CSharp` 4.14.0 (the repo's pinned version, `Directory.Packages.props:23`). No repository file was edited. The probe compiles the live `analyzers/AgentGuard.Analyzers` sources from disk, applies mutations to in-memory copies, and never writes back.

The analyzer-source model, measured: 82 source files. Compiled with no synthetic global-usings tree → 156 compiler errors (CS0246 ×66, CS0103 ×62, CS1503 ×26, CS1955 ×2), because `Directory.Build.props:15` sets `ImplicitUsings=enable`. Prepending one 7-line synthetic `global using` tree (System, Collections.Generic, IO, Linq, Net.Http, Threading, Threading.Tasks) → 83 trees, **0 errors**. Cost, end to end: parse+compile 358 ms, diagnostics 1111 ms, registrations 591 ms (114 `Register*` calls), call graph 803 ms (376 methods, 479 intra-project edges), report sites 421 ms (51 sites). ~3.3 s for the whole model and every query.

Registration ownership, symbol-resolved (each argument bound to its `IFieldSymbol` on `SymbolKind`/`OperationKind`/`SyntaxKind`, reading through kind-carrying fields so `MemberUseScanner.MemberUseKinds` is read through, not past):
- Exactly one declaring type registers `SymbolKind.Field` AND `Property` AND `Method` together: `ContractConcreteTypeMustNotBeReferencedAnalyzer`.
- Exactly four register two of the three: `NoCoverageOptOutAnalyzer` {Method, NamedType, Property}, `NoStateInNativeOpsAnalyzer` {Event, Field, NamedType, Property}, `NoStaticServiceHolderAnalyzer` {Field, Property}, `ReturnTypesMustNotBeTuplesAnalyzer` {Method, NamedType, Property}.
- `OperationKind.VariableDeclarator`: one owner (AG0006). `SyntaxKind.IdentifierName`/`GenericName`: zero owners.
- `MemberUseScanner.RegisterForAssembly` has exactly two callers today, both `BoundaryAssembly.Name` (`BoundariesToCrossPlatformOneDoorAnalyzer.cs:66`, `BoundariesToPerOsOneDoorAnalyzer.cs:58`).

`ContainingSymbol` has 7 reads, all already flowing into `CompositionPoint` or `OwnerClass` (`GuardedConstructionAnalyzer.cs:127,137,151`, `OwnerClass.cs:36`, `PresenceCheckOnlyFromApprovalGateAnalyzer.cs:82`, `TempRootBackDoorAnalyzer.cs:92`, `TimeMustUseTimeProviderAnalyzer.cs:71`). `GetEnclosingSymbol` has none. `TypeTree.Any` has two callers (`ContractPattern.cs:50`, `ReturnTypesMustNotBeTuplesAnalyzer.cs:131`).

A Roslyn analyzer cannot police the analyzer project: `Directory.Build.props:84` wires AgentGuard's analyzers only where `AgentGuardIsAnalyzerProject != 'true'`, and `AgentGuard.Analyzers.csproj` sets it true. Every architecture check below is therefore a test.

=====================================================================
B. THE RESPONSIBILITIES, THEIR FILES, AND THEIR C# INTERFACES
=====================================================================

B1. "Resolve a written node to the symbol it binds to and the type that name denotes, recovering the type when the symbol does not bind."

This is the mechanic `AttributeIdentity.ResolveAttributeType` (`AttributeIdentity.cs:60-72`) already owns for attributes and `ContractConcreteTypeMustNotBeCastToAnalyzer.Check` (`:84`) owns for a `TypeSyntax`. Neither can own it for the other, and `WrittenNameScanner` needs both halves. It becomes `analyzers/AgentGuard.Analyzers/SymbolResolution.cs`:

```csharp
internal static class SymbolResolution
{
    internal static (ISymbol? Symbol, INamedTypeSymbol? Type) Resolve(
        SemanticModel semanticModel, SyntaxNode node, CancellationToken cancellationToken);

    internal static INamedTypeSymbol? DenotedType(ISymbol? symbol);

    internal static INamedTypeSymbol? RecoveredType(
        SemanticModel semanticModel, SyntaxNode node, CancellationToken cancellationToken);
}
```

`Resolve` = `GetSymbolInfo(...).Symbol`, then `DenotedType(bound) ?? RecoveredType(...)`. `DenotedType(s)` is `(s as INamedTypeSymbol ?? s?.ContainingType)` filtered to `TypeKind: not TypeKind.Error`. `RecoveredType` is the `GetTypeInfo` tier.

`AttributeIdentity.ResolveAttributeType` collapses to `SymbolResolution.Resolve(semanticModel, attribute, cancellationToken).Type`. MEASURED equivalent on every spelling: `[Guarded(1)]` (ctor binds), `[Guarded]`, `[N.Guarded]`, `[GuardedAttribute]` (all three with the required argument omitted, so `GetSymbolInfo` is null and only the type binds), `[Guarded2]` (no-arg ctor), and `[Undefined]` — current and shared agree on all six, including returning null for the undefined identifier so the syntactic fallback still runs exactly where it runs today. `AttributeIdentity` keeps `IsAnyOf` and `MatchesSyntactically`: the attribute-specific matching and the fail-closed syntactic fallback policy stay with it, as settled. AG0008 and AG0105 are behaviourally unchanged.

`ContractConcreteTypeMustNotBeCastToAnalyzer` is NOT in Surfaces and is not touched; it stays as it is.

B2. The three lenses.

`MemberUseScanner` — RETAINED, unchanged. `Register` (`MemberUseScanner.cs:43`) and `RegisterForAssembly` (`:61`) are used as they stand by AG0040 (Engine gate), AG0041 (both consumer gates), and AG0023/AG0029 (Boundaries gate unchanged, plus the new Engine gate). Owns calls, `new`, property/field reads, method groups.

`DeclaredTypeScanner` — EXTRACTED from `ContractConcreteTypeMustNotBeReferencedAnalyzer.cs:49-52` (the four registrations) and `:55-102` (the four handlers). Owns "the types a declaration carries without naming them."

```csharp
internal readonly struct DeclaredType
{
    internal DeclaredType(ITypeSymbol type, Location location, ISymbol containingSymbol,
        SyntaxNode? site, Action<Diagnostic> report);

    internal ITypeSymbol Type { get; }
    internal Location Location { get; }
    internal ISymbol ContainingSymbol { get; }   // the call-site symbol the caller test needs
    internal SyntaxNode? Site { get; }           // the syntax the caller test needs (lambda/local-function walk)
    internal Action<Diagnostic> Report { get; }  // SymbolAnalysisContext and OperationAnalysisContext share no base
}

internal static class DeclaredTypeScanner
{
    internal static readonly ImmutableArray<SymbolKind> DeclarationKinds;   // Field, Property, Method

    internal static void Register(CompilationStartAnalysisContext context, Action<DeclaredType> inspect);
    internal static void RegisterForAssembly(
        CompilationStartAnalysisContext context, string assemblyName, Action<DeclaredType> inspect);

    internal static IEnumerable<(ITypeSymbol Type, Location Location)> CarriedTypes(ISymbol symbol);
}
```

`CarriedTypes` is the whole judgement, pure and directly callable — that is what the direct scanner tests drive, and it is what keeps the four per-position locations identical to AG0006's today (method location for a bad return type, parameter location for a parameter, `Locations[0]` for field/property/local). AG0006's `Initialize` becomes one `RegisterCompilationStartAction` plus a four-line `Inspect` applying its existing `ContractPattern.ReferencesContractImplementation` leaf test. Acceptance 13 is preserved.

`WrittenNameScanner` — NEW. Owns "every name the source writes, as the symbol it binds to."

```csharp
internal static class WrittenNameScanner
{
    internal static readonly ImmutableArray<SyntaxKind> NameKinds;  // IdentifierName, GenericName

    internal static void Register(
        CompilationStartAnalysisContext context,
        Action<SyntaxNodeAnalysisContext, ISymbol, INamedTypeSymbol> inspect);

    internal static void RegisterForAssembly(
        CompilationStartAnalysisContext context, string assemblyName,
        Action<SyntaxNodeAnalysisContext, ISymbol, INamedTypeSymbol> inspect);

    internal static bool IsDocumentationReference(SyntaxNode node);
}
```

It hands back BOTH the bound symbol and the denoted type, because AG0041 governs internal Engine MEMBERS as well as types. `RegisterForAssembly` reuses `OwnerClass.InAssembly` (`OwnerClass.cs:107`), the existing owner of the compilation-assembly-name comparison, rather than a third inline string compare.

MEASURED coverage of the lens, through a real `CompilationWithAnalyzers` over a fixture carrying every contract-named position (typeof, nameof, cast, `as`, `is` pattern, generic argument, generic constraint, base list, attribute argument, using alias and its use, array element, field/property/parameter/return/local declaration, inferred `var`, lambda, local function, event): the driver visits **70 of the 71** name nodes in the tree. The single miss is the LEFT segment of a namespace declaration's dotted name (`Outer` in `namespace Outer.Inner`); the rightmost segment and every `using` directive segment are visited. A namespace segment never denotes a type, so the miss costs nothing — but it is a real hole and belongs in the lens's own documentation, not in a claim of total coverage.

B3. The documentation-reference exclusion.

The discriminator is `node.FirstAncestorOrSelf<CrefSyntax>() is not null`.

Proof it excludes documentation references and nothing else: `CrefSyntax` is the base of the six cref forms, and the C# grammar admits a `CrefSyntax` only as the value of an `XmlCrefAttributeSyntax`, which exists only inside a `DocumentationCommentTriviaSyntax`. There is no executable position with a `CrefSyntax` ancestor. Measured on a `guard` fixture carrying the real production comment text: every node the discriminator excludes is a cref name; every executable-position node is `cref=false`; `<paramref>`/`<param>` names are `cref=false` and bind to `IParameterSymbol`, whose denoted type under `SymbolResolution.DenotedType` is the parameter's own containing type — always a type declared in the compilation under analysis, therefore never an Engine internal reached from `guard`, and never a CrossPlatform or per-OS type reached from Engine. So the narrower `CrefSyntax` test is sufficient, and the broader "anywhere in a doc comment" test is not needed.

End-to-end proof on the live production text (the `Program.cs:17` and `:53` comments, plus an application-code `typeof(SystemServices)`, over an internal Engine fake carrying both `InternalsVisibleTo` grants, 0 compiler errors in both compilations):
- exclusion ON → **1** diagnostic: the application-code `typeof(SystemServices)`.
- exclusion OFF → **3** diagnostics: the same one plus both production doc references.

That is the requested test pair, and it is also the measured production impact the withdrawn `<c>…</c>` rewrite was papering over.

Also measured, and load-bearing for the test model: the driver visits doc-comment names under `DocumentationMode.Parse` (14 nodes) and `Diagnose` (14) and not under `None` (8). `CSharpSyntaxTree.ParseText(source)` defaults to `Parse`, and the production build sets `GenerateDocumentationFile=true` → `Diagnose`. So an `AnalyzerRunner` fixture carrying a doc comment reproduces production exactly, with no runner change. A `<c>SystemServices</c>` span is never a name node at all — which is why the withdrawn rewrite "worked": it deleted the subject.

## 3. THE CREF EXCLUSION

**Discriminator:** `name.FirstAncestorOrSelf<CrefSyntax>() is not null`.

**Proof it excludes documentation and nothing else.** A `CrefSyntax` is producible only inside XML documentation trivia — there is no other syntax context in C# that yields one. Measured on a fixture with five documentation references (`<see cref="Guarded"/>`, `<see cref="Guarded.Member"/>` as two nodes, `<see cref="Holder.Take(Guarded)"/>`, `<seealso cref="Guarded"/>`) and nine application-code references (parameter type, attribute application, `typeof`, `is` pattern, local declaration, member access ×3, malformed attribute): all five documentation nodes have a `CrefSyntax` ancestor, all nine application-code nodes have none. `name.Parent is CrefSyntax` fails on the cref-parameter form, so the ancestor walk is the correct test, not the parent test.

**Why it is in the lens, not in the three consumers.** All three consumers need the identical exclusion; spelling it three times is the duplication the rest of this design exists to prevent. `MemberUseScanner` and `DeclaredTypeScanner` never see crefs — a cref produces no operation and no symbol declaration — so `WrittenNameScanner` is the one place the exclusion can live and the only place it can be needed.

**What the exclusion costs, plainly.** A guarded type or internal Engine member named only inside a cref is never reported. That is exactly the intent: a cref compiles to no IL and reaches no member, so it is documentation, not access. What is given up: if the referenced type is later renamed or made unreachable, the compiler reports CS1574 and the guard says nothing — documentation drift becomes the compiler's problem, not the guard's. Nothing else changes; the exclusion turns on syntax context alone and cannot be widened by anything written in application code.

The failure is a loud red, not a silent pass, and D is scoped to report sites in `OneDoorRule`.

Check D cannot prove the guard is the APPROVED predicate. Three mutations measured green against every structural check: an extra narrowing predicate AND-ed onto the owner (rule accepts less than approved), the owner called with the wrong argument (accepts nothing), and the owner OR-ed with a copied check (accepts more than approved). The second is covered by the Acceptance 2 positive tests and the third by the decoy caller fixtures; the FIRST is covered by nothing if the narrowing happens to accept every fixture. That residue is irreducible and must be stated in the test file, never papered over. Weakening the Acceptance-12 or decoy fixture sets removes the only real proof while the architecture test still passes.

The written-name lens fires `GetSymbolInfo` on every `IdentifierName` and `GenericName` node in three gated compilations — `AgentGuard.Engine`, `guard`, `AgentGuard.TestHelpers`. Build-time cost on a real Engine compile is UNMEASURED. The assembly gate runs first and the cref test is syntactic, but RULE-PHASE must record the before/after build-time delta on those three compilations and report it rather than assume it unchanged.

The lens misses one name position: the LEFT segment of a namespace declaration's dotted name (70 of 71 nodes visited, measured on two independently shaped fixtures). A namespace segment never denotes a type so nothing escapes, but the miss goes in `WrittenNameScanner`'s own doc comment rather than being left as an implied claim of total coverage.

The cref exclusion is a real hole by design: inside the gated compilations a documentation comment may name any guarded type or member freely, from any method including a decoy, and no rule any longer proves documentation stays off a forbidden path. It is bounded — a cref produces no operation, so no use hides behind one, and the compiler still requires it to bind (CS1574, an error under the verified `TreatWarningsAsErrors=true`) — but it is a hole and it is the price of preserving the three live links unchanged.

`AnalyzerRunner` parses with `CSharpSyntaxTree.ParseText(source)` and no options (verified at :54, :90, :98, :124), giving `DocumentationMode.Parse`, while the production build uses `Diagnose` via the verified `GenerateDocumentationFile=true`. Both visit and bind crefs, so fixtures reproduce production. If the runner's parse options ever became `None`, every documentation test would pass vacuously — mitigated by each test asserting a `CrefSyntax` node exists first, and the risk survives only if that assertion is removed. The contract forbids changing `AnalyzerRunner.cs`, so this is a watch item, not a defect.

An inferred `var` identifier binds to the inferred type, so a `var` local of a guarded type reports through BOTH type lenses, and `SystemServices.Create()` fires the written-name lens twice. Every exact count in the four analyzer test classes must be computed from the lens matrix. A test author who assumes one diagnostic per declaration will write the wrong number and then 'fix' the rule to match; an `Assert.Single` anywhere in those classes passes today and hides a lens that stopped firing tomorrow.

The wrong-ASSEMBLY half of the CALLER identity is not reachable behaviourally — a call site's enclosing method is always in the compilation under analysis, and Acceptance 4 requires nothing reported from a non-Engine compilation. It is proved by one direct `CompositionPoint.IsContainerFactory` assertion, and the test file must say that this is the only available proof, or a later reader will read it as a weaker substitute and try to replace it with a fixture that cannot pass.

`PlatformFactory.Is` anchors AG0029's door on namespace plus name through `WellKnownType.Is` (verified at PlatformFactory.cs:41), NOT on the declaring assembly; the per-OS assembly scope gate covers the assembly half for the callee. That is existing approved behaviour and out of scope here, but AG0029's decoy tests must be written against that actual shape or they will assert something the rule does not do.

`MemberUseScanner.cs:66-70` spells the compilation-assembly-name comparison inline, duplicating what `OwnerClass.InAssembly` (verified at OwnerClass.cs:107) owns. The two new `RegisterForAssembly` gates route through `OwnerClass.InAssembly` so they do not become a third copy, but the existing copy stays because the contract's reuse ledger freezes MemberUseScanner ('It is used unchanged'). A DRY adversary will see two spellings; the reason is contractual, not a miss, and must be recorded as such.

`AnalyzerSourceModel` depends on `Directory.Build.props` keeping `ImplicitUsings=enable` (verified) and on the SDK's implicit using set staying what the synthesized tree spells, which makes that tree a SECOND place the implicit set is written down and it must carry a comment saying so. It also builds its reference set from the test process's trusted platform assemblies, so a CI image with a different set could reintroduce errors — a loud red leg with no local repro rather than a wrong answer.

The model compiles the analyzer project's `netstandard2.0` sources against the net10.0 assemblies loaded in the test process. The zero-error gate makes any mismatch loud, but a future package or TFM bump turns that gate red for a reason unrelated to this design, and the failure will read as an ownership failure unless the assertion message says otherwise.

Check D's never-read-local detection calls `SemanticModel.AnalyzeDataFlow`, which throws when the node is not inside a statement body — an expression-bodied member or a field initializer. The check must handle the expression-bodied form explicitly; `OneDoorRule` would hold the only call site today, so the gap would not show until someone writes an expression-bodied consumer.

`ILocalSymbol.ContainingSymbol` is measured correct for a local in a method body, a lambda and a local function. It is NOT measured for a local inside a lambda in a field or property initializer, or under top-level statements. Engine has none today; a fixture covering the field-initializer lambda should be added rather than assuming the answer.

`analyzers/AgentGuard.Analyzers.Tests/SharedAnalyzerSources.cs` already exists in the working tree (verified, 16 029 bytes, commit c1c2a18) while the contract's Surfaces lists it as a new file, and `AttributeIdentity.cs` and `PlatformFactory.cs` are edited by this design but are not in Surfaces at all. A worker reading Surfaces literally creates a second shared-fixtures file or overwrites 16 KB, and the two unlisted edits are out-of-contract changes REFUTE will flag. Both must be fixed in the contract before RULE-PHASE.

Placing the cref exclusion inside `WrittenNameScanner` folds an access-enforcement policy into a lens. It is right for the three rules that exist — all three are access rules and none could want a documentation reference — but it is a design element that outlives its function, so it is recorded as a decision rather than taken silently.
